description:
## Problem
CI on PR #280 (ubuntu x86_64) kills the fz lib test binary with a plain SIGSEGV, with no 'has overflowed its stack' line, at the exec::runtime raise tests. macOS arm64 and Linux arm64 pass.

The try emission (src/compiler2/native_codegen/terminator.rs, emit_try) builds the handler template with ContinuationPlan::heap_closure(..).emit_value, which yields a closure *reference word*: the heap tag sits in the high bits (bit 56 on arm64, bit 57 on x86_64, see AnyValueRefPacking in runtime/src/any_value.rs) and the low four bits are zero. fz_try_push (runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs) converts with closure_addr_from_tagged, which recognises only the low-tagged *object word* form, so the match fails and unwrap_or stores the reference word itself inside Handler::Closure(ClosureRef). On a raise, failure.rs::raise passes template.as_ptr() to materialize_outcome_closure (runtime/src/park.rs), which dereferences that word as an address. Arm64's top-byte-ignore makes the dereference land on the right object; on x86_64 the word is non-canonical and the load faults. A collection between the push and the raise launders the word (closure_root falls back to AnyValue::heap_ptr, which masks the tag), which is why only an un-collected first raise shows it.

The receive path converts its words with closure_addr_from_ref_word (fz_receive_park_matched); fz_try_push must do the same. The existing unit test (runtime/src/ir_runtime_test.rs ~775) pushes only the object-word and bare-pointer forms, never the form codegen emits.

## Change
- fz_try_push takes the closure reference word codegen emits and converts it with closure_addr_from_ref_word, strictly: no unwrap_or fallback, any other form panics with the context, loud. Doc comment says what the argument is.
- Handler::Closure holds a heap address, as ClosureRef documents, from the moment it is pushed.

## Acceptance
- Unit test in runtime/src/ir_runtime_test.rs: pushing the reference word of a heap closure (heap_ref_word(CLOSURE, addr) form, as fz_alloc_closure returns) stores a handler whose as_ptr() equals the closure's address. Red before the change on arm64 (stored word carries the tag bits), green after.
- The lib test binary cross-built for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu runs the exec::runtime raise tests under an amd64 container without a fault (coordinator verifies; this is the CI failure).
- Full gate green: RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 cargo test --workspace --all-targets, cargo test --workspace --doc, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --all -- --check.
- Fixture census and goldens unchanged.
- .agent/docs/exceptions.md states the handler template's representation at push (a closure reference word from codegen, held as a heap address on the handler stack).
title: A handler template is stored by its heap address on every architecture
